sense: the top, middle, bottom, end or rest of a thing
also: in the middle of the night
at the top of the page

terms.gloss: the top of: the top of the tree, the top of the hill
terms.grammar: adjective, agreeing with the noun for the whole
terms.comment: Latin says “the highest tree” for “the top of the tree”: in summā arbore, at the top of the tree; summus mōns, the top of the mountain. So with every word here: the part is an adjective agreeing with the whole, not a noun with a genitive.

terms.gloss: the middle of: the middle of the night, of the road
evidence: Gell. 3.2.2: ā mediā nocte ad proximam mediam noctem
terms.comment: media nox, the middle of the night, midnight; in mediā viā, in the middle of the road (see centre).

terms.gloss: the bottom of, the foot of
terms.comment: in īmīs collibus, at the foot of the hills.

terms.gloss: the end of, the far edge of
terms.comment: The farthest part of a place, or the last of a time; ultimus is used the same way.
agmen reliquum, the rest of the column; for the others besides those named, cēterī (see the rest).

terms.gloss: the beginning of, the front of
a great part of, most of
terms.grammar: noun phrase, with the genitive of the whole
terms.comment: Here the genitive is right, because pars is a noun (see most).

terms.gloss: the middle of (a noun with a genitive)
terms.register: vōx plērumque poētica: Ov.; in ōrātiōne solūtā posterior
terms.comment: Poetry and later prose; in plain speech say media nox.

phrases.english: The cat is sitting at the top of the tree.
It’s the middle of the night now; go to sleep.

phrases.latin: in summā Sacrā viā fuit posita virgō īnsidēns equō
phrases.english: at the top of the Sacred Way was set up a girl sitting on a horse

phrases.latin: modicus prīmō labor in īmīs collibus fuit
phrases.english: at first the toil at the foot of the hills was moderate

phrases.latin: prīmā deinde lūce castra mōta et agmen reliquum incēdere coepit
phrases.english: then at first light the camp was struck, and the rest of the column began to move

phrases.latin: quī inde ā mediā nocte ad proximam mediam noctem … nātī sunt
phrases.english: those born from one midnight to the next
whether he makes his way to the farthest Indians

phrases.latin: noctis erat medium placidīque silentia somnī
phrases.english: it was the middle of the night, and the silence of peaceful sleep

phrases.latin: magna pars vītae ēlābitur male agentibus, maxima nihil agentibus, tōta vīta aliud agentibus
phrases.english: a great part of life slips away from those who do wrong, most of it from those who do nothing, the whole of it from those who do something else
at the top of the page
